bias_caveat: IMPORTANT: Facial emotion recognition (DeepFace) has documented accuracy disparities across skin tone and gender (Buolamwini & Gebru, 2018; Fan et al., 2023). Authenticity scores informed by facial data should be interpreted with this limitation in mind.
vocal_caveat: IMPORTANT: The vocal emotion channel is the second weakest of the four, after facial emotion, and is explicitly down-weighted. Benchmarked on 150 hand-rated clips from 6 speakers (vocal_bench/), the adopted model scores 48.9% three-class accuracy on held-out speakers - better than the model it replaced, which at 34.0% was significantly worse than always guessing NEUTRAL (p = 0.0070), but still not reliably better than that constant. No model tested beat it. Conflicts attributed to the vocal channel alone are damped accordingly, and per-segment claims should not rest on this channel. Read the within-video figure, not the headline: this report compares segments inside one video, and the channel's rank correlation with human judgement measured within a video is +0.159 across 147 clips and +0.056 on unseen speakers (vocal_bench/SPEAKER_NORM_RESULT.md). Most of its apparent accuracy is a between-video effect that says more about the speaker's habitual energy than about any individual moment.
vocal_licence_note: The adopted vocal model (audeering/wav2vec2-large-robust-12-ft-emotion-msp-dim) is licensed CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 and may not be used commercially. Every configuration measured in vocal_bench/ that showed usable signal was non-commercially licensed; the permissively-licensed alternatives measured at the bottom of every table. A commercial deployment would need to ship without this channel or replace it.

Great video as always. 

Here a few comments and questions that I have that I don’t see anyone talking about that I’d love your thoughts on:

1. On paper, there are a few solid features that the iPhone Duo has that the Galaxy Z Fold 8 doesn’t. Namely: a vapor chamber, IP68 rated, flex mode, under-display interior camera. I think those are the main key differences.

2. The Z Fold 8 is quite a bit thinner and lighter. 

3. The main thing I’m concerned about with the Duo is the following: Samsung is extremely customizable. And for a folding phone with several possible form factors like the Duo and Z Fold 8, having the ability to customize how things work and where things go, to me, feels like an absolute must. Here are two small examples of things that I’m assuming the Duo won’t be able to do, but for me, seem like things that will make the Duo difficult for many people to use. When holding the phone with your right hand, one handed, for most people, reaching the left side of the outer display will be very difficult. On the Z Fold 8, there are two ways of overcoming that. 1. The back gesture can be on the right side. 2. One handed mode. Another thing. When open, if you want to use it with one hand, Samsung’s one handed mode is excellent. I’m sure the duo won’t have that. Then take the fact that you can have the inner display remain different than the outer display, giving you effectively two different devices, I’m sure the duo won’t have that. 

These are just a few of my thoughts. I’d love to hear yours!

all_segments.text: Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, is official. I've had some early hands-on time,
and also got to test some of the cameras, and here's everything you need to know.
So first up, it's a passport size when it is closed.
It's something we were expecting. And it comes in two colors, a night sky,
which is similar to the blue from the iPhone 17 Pro series,
and a star wide. The left side is flat when it's closed,
and the right side has some curves, and when you open it, then you've got curves on all four corners.
Now, it does feel very premium. We've got grade five titanium for the frame,
as well as some components in the hinge, with ceramic shield two on the front,
and ceramic shield on the back. Now, the frame is glossy like we had on the iPhone Air,
so very fingerprinty, but it is IP68 water and dust resistant.
So this is the same water and dust resistant rating that we've got on your regular iPhones.
Now, size-wise, so when it's open,
it's 5.2 millimeters, making it the thinnest iPhone ever.
And when it's closed, it's around 11.3 millimeters,
weighs around 254 grams. So when we do compare it to others out there,
like the Z Fold 8, then those are definitely a lot more compact.
Just to give you some context, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 weighs around 201 grams,
and it's around 4.5 millimeters when it's unfolded.
Now, of course, there are going to be lots of comparisons drawn in particular with the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8,
and I am going to be working on a SuperSaf style comparison
between the two when the iPhone Duo is officially out.
So if you want to see that first, be sure to subscribe and hit that bell icon.
Now, to put the weight in context, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is around 249 grams,
so pretty similar to the iPhone 18 Pro Max. Now, let's talk about the displays.
So Apple are calling the displays the outer display
and inner display, not the cover and main display, like a lot of Android manufacturers do.
The outer display is around 5.4 inches.
The inner display is 7.6 inches.
Now, both displays are very bright, around 3,000 nits of HDR peak brightness,
but the inner display has a nano-texture coating,
and this really minimizes the crease.
Now, of course, Apple has done lots of engineering to minimize that crease,
but in particular, with that nano-texture, it completely minimizes it,
and it looks very impressive in person. Is the crease completely gone?
Probably not. You can still see it at certain angles, but it is absolutely minimal.
If you're thinking of upgrading to one of the new iPhones, don't downgrade your experience
with a cheap case or screen protector. ESR soft vegan leather cases look sleek,
feel premium, and can resist daily stains with effortless cleanup.
I love the dual-function flex and 180-degree rotating stand,
which can be used when your iPhone is folded or unfolded,
and in portrait or landscape. ESR screen protectors use accessory glass by Corning,
the same glass supplier of iPhone screens, giving you 10 times the impact absorption
and two times better scratch performance compared to generic tempered glass screen protectors.
And the UltraFit tray ensures perfect alignment
with dust and bubble-free installation in one simple port.
Check out the link in the description to see all of the new ESR iPhone cases and screen protectors,
and make sure you're protected as soon as you get your new iPhone. Now, being an Apple device, I think one of the key things
is just how everything works, and Apple has really focused on the software
to make everything as fluid as possible. When we are on the cover screen,
instead of having some of the controls towards the bottom, they are now on the side, the essential controls.
And then when you open the device, you get this really smooth, fluid animation.
The outer display is then mirrored to the right-hand side of the inner display,
keeping everything consistent, so things are not moving around,
and they're exactly in the same place as they were on the outer display before you unfolded it.
Now, when you have it open, obviously you have a big canvas. It's almost like having an iPad mini.
You can view this in portrait, which is great for things like websites and books.
And when you've got it in landscape, then of course you can multitask. And this works pretty well.
You can just be in any app and just drag from the bottom,
and then snap it either to the left or the right. You can even switch through apps on one side of the screen,
which is pretty cool. And then you also have different modes. So the hinge is pretty strong,
and you can have, Samsung call it flex mode. Apple have their own names for it.
We've got seated, which is where you can have it halfway
and have, say, a video playing on the top half and have the controls at the bottom half.
But then when you flip it, then you can have it standing. And this is where you can potentially watch some movies
or anything like that. And you can also have it in standby mode.
So you can display the clock and some of your widgets and things. Apple has worked with some third-party developers as well.
So the Netflix apps, for example, works great on all of the different modes and displays.
It's quite intuitive how it switches between all of them. Now, one thing which is pretty cool
is that both the outer and inner display
will have support for the Apple Pencil
coming later this year. I'm not sure when, and I'm not sure why it's delayed,
but will they have a separate Apple Pencil, like a different one that can maybe go into a case
or something? I don't know, but hey, Samsung, if Apple can do it, then what's your excuse?
I get it. Your phone's thinner, but still, come on. Now let's talk about the cameras.
And this is maybe why Apple didn't call this the Ultra
and called it the Duo, because it has two rear-facing cameras,
not three like the Pro devices. So the primary camera is different to the iPhone 18 Pro
and Pro Max. It is 48 megapixels with an F1.6 aperture.
Then we have a 48 megapixel ultra wide camera, which is actually the same as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
And then we have two selfie cameras. So there is a 12 megapixel center stage selfie camera
on the outside screen. But on the inside screen,
we have an under display FaceTime camera.
Now the key thing here is Apple are calling this FaceTime camera.
They didn't actually specify the megapixels. As far as I can see, it's around four megapixels.
And as the name suggests, it is really only supposed to be used for videos
rather than photos. So as you can see a side-by-side from the outer
and the inner cameras. And also you can use the rear-facing cameras
as selfie cameras. So we've got a few different modes. One of them is called Smart Take.
So you can prop up the iPhone Duo. And then if you go in front of it,
it's going to try to detect when you make a pose, or you change position and it's going to try to
intelligently take those moments. And then we've got dual preview.
So then you can use the outer screen to preview
what you've got from the rear-facing cameras. Now this can be used from both the primary
as well as the ultra-wide camera. If you've got a lot of people in your shots, there's one feature called Kid Q,
where you can have like an animation playing to get the attention of the child.
And this is going to use the outer display camera,
selfie camera to take that picture. And you've also got dual FaceTime.
So you can have somebody that's behind you and yourself
on a FaceTime call together when you are calling somebody. Now when it comes to the features,
we do have all of the new features. So we have manual controls, finally.
Finally, Apple is giving manual controls within the camera app.
This is going to put a lot of third-party apps out of business, but you can now control things
like your exposure and your white balance and things
right from within your app. And then you can also customize these and pin them.
We've got the third generation of photographic styles. I'm a big fan of photographic styles.
It really allows you to customize your pictures after you've taken them.
Now, in addition to tone and color, you can also customize texture and grain.
And cinematic mode also gets an update. So you can just take a regular video
and then you can turn it into a cinematic video after the fact.
Now you may have noticed that there is no dynamic island.
There is just a punch out for the selfie camera
on the outer display. And that is because we do not have face ID.
This is something we were kind of expecting, trying to get all of that tech in there.
And instead there is touch ID on the side. Not sure how you guys feel about that
because touch ID has been gone for so long on iPhones. And now it's back here on the iPhone duo.
I personally don't mind it. And the volume buttons are placed at the top.
Now, this is actually pretty clever because when you are trying to take a selfie
from the rear facing cameras, they're pretty accessible.
The only thing I would say is if you are taking a selfie from the ultra wide camera,
your finger can cover the camera a little bit if you are trying to press one of those volume buttons.
The speakers, we've got speakers on the bottom of the top, but they're on the opposite side.
So when the iPhone duo is folded out,
then you're still going to get relatively good sound. It's not just going to be off to one side.
Now for the software, of course, we've got iOS 27 with Apple intelligence.
And we've got all of the new Apple intelligence features, such as Siri AI, which understands personal context.
And of course, all the photo editing features are still here. So we've got cleanup, we've got extend,
as well as spatial reframe, which are also going to be available
on the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max. Now for performance, we do have the A20 Pro chip.
Now, as far as I can see, this is pretty much exactly the same
as what we've got on the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.
So that means overall, it's going to be up to 20% faster than the A19 Pro, and it's going to have up to 50%
more memory bandwidth than the A19 Pro, with up to 35% higher sustained performance
than the iPhone 17 Pro. Now, I would expect the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max
to give better performance overall, because they have a bigger vapor chamber and better cooling,
